The earlier cumulative test failed only on 8%-coverage cash-flow lines and with a profitability rather than a liquidity conditioner, so this is a substantively different test rather than a rerun.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Near Term Funding Gap In Revenue Months
considered.expression: WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(ADD(dlc, SUB(DELTA(SUB(act, che), 1), dp)), che), sale), 1)
considered.hypothesis: Accruals and distress can be expressed in the same units — dollars of cash the firm must find — so the economically primitive quantity is maturing debt plus the incremental cash absorbed by soft working capital (net of the depreciation shield) less the cash already on hand, measured against annual revenue; firms with a large gap must either refinance, liquidate soft assets at a discount, or issue equity.
considered.reasoning: This replaces the diagnostic product with an additive, units-consistent funding-requirement construct in which the two themes are not multiplied but summed as competing claims on the same cash, a functional form absent from the archive. Deflating by sales rather than by book equity avoids the near-zero-denominator microcap distortion the critic identified in the cushion ratio while keeping a stable, broadly reported scale.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Funding Gap Net Of Internal Cash Generation
considered.expression: RANK(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(ADD(dlc, SUB(DELTA(SUB(act, che), 1), dp)), ADD(che, oancf)), sale), 1))
considered.hypothesis: A firm facing maturing debt and a working-capital drain is only in trouble if operations cannot fund it, so subtracting operating cash flow alongside the cash stock converts the gap from a balance-sheet snapshot into a true external-financing requirement.
considered.reasoning: This isolates one design choice against signal 1 — whether internal cash generation belongs in the sources term — and it is exactly the variable that separates a growing, self-funding firm with high accruals from a fragile one that must go to the capital markets. It also sharpens the accrual interpretation, because a firm whose reported earnings are accrual-driven will show a large gap precisely when oancf fails to cover the claim.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Widening Funding Gap
considered.expression: RANK(WINSOR(DELTA(RATIO(SUB(ADD(dlc, SUB(DELTA(SUB(act, che), 1), dp)), che), sale), 1), 1))
considered.hypothesis: Markets price the level of a liquidity shortfall slowly but may miss its deterioration entirely; a gap that widened over the past year identifies firms whose accrual absorption and refinancing needs are growing faster than their revenue base, which is the state that precedes covenant breach and dilutive issuance.
considered.reasoning: Level versus change is a genuine and unresolved lesson in this archive — conditioning on rising leverage worked (alpha −2.8%, t = −3.24) while the level of leverage worked less well — and here it is tested on the construct with the strongest portfolio evidence. A change specification also purges persistent firm characteristics such as capital intensity and industry turnover that the level ratio inevitably carries.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Unbacked Earnings Meeting A Funding Gap
considered.expression: MIN(ZSCORE(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(ib, oancf), at), 1)), ZSCORE(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(ADD(dlc, SUB(DELTA(SUB(act, che), 1), dp)), che), sale), 1)))
considered.hypothesis: The most dangerous firm is the one whose reported profit is not backed by cash *and* which must find cash within the year; either condition alone is survivable, but their conjunction means the accounting story and the funding reality are about to collide.
considered.reasoning: MIN of two demeaned legs flags only firms failing both tests and is not a monotone reweighting of either, and the earlier MIN construction already delivered a significant alpha, so this tests whether pairing the funding gap with a pure earnings-quality measure adds to the gap alone. The two legs use different accounting primitives — income versus cash flow on one side, balance-sheet claims on the other — so there is no mechanical overlap driving the conjunction.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Accrual Turbulence Under Rollover Pressure
considered.expression: MUL(ZSCORE(WINSOR(ABS(RATIO(SUB(DELTA(ADD(SUB(wcap, che), dlc), 1), dp), at)), 1)), RANK(RATIO(dlc, lt)))
considered.hypothesis: For a firm with debt coming due, any large swing in working capital is a warning — an unusual build means cash is trapped in soft assets, while an unusual liquidation means the firm is already harvesting receivables and inventory to make payments — so the magnitude of the accrual, regardless of direction, should predict underperformance under liquidity pressure.
considered.reasoning: Every archive signal assumes a monotone accrual effect, yet the distress mechanism implies a non-monotone one: forced working-capital liquidation by a constrained firm is bad news even though it registers as a large negative accrual. Testing the absolute value against the same conditioner as the archive's best signal cleanly identifies whether the relation is one-sided or U-shaped, which determines how the whole family should be built from here.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Funding Gap Extreme Versus Peers And Own History
considered.expression: SUMRANK(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(ADD(dlc, SUB(DELTA(SUB(act, che), 1), dp)), che), sale), 1), TS_RANK(RATIO(SUB(ADD(dlc, SUB(DELTA(SUB(act, che), 1), dp)), che), sale), 5))
considered.hypothesis: A firm is genuinely in trouble when its near-term cash requirement is high both relative to other firms and relative to the way it has financed itself for the past five years; structurally gap-heavy business models are priced, but a firm sitting at the top of its own five-year gap distribution is experiencing a new and unpriced deterioration.
considered.reasoning: This is not a monotone re-expression of the archived gap: adding the firm's own time-series position materially reorders the cross-section, demoting low-turnover firms that always carry a large gap and promoting firms whose accrual absorption and maturing debt have just spiked. It also directly addresses the suspicion that the sale-deflated gap's alpha comes from a persistent business-model tilt rather than from a distress event, because the second leg is purely within-firm.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Accruals While Creditors Shorten The Leash
considered.expression: MUL(ZSCORE(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(DELTA(ADD(SUB(wcap, che), dlc), 1), dp), at), 1)), RANK(NEG(DELTA(RATIO(dltt, lt), 1))))
considered.hypothesis: Distress is revealed by the credit supply side: when the long-term share of a firm's liabilities falls, lenders are refusing to term out its debt, and accrual-heavy earnings reported in the same year are precisely the earnings that cannot be validated with cash before the shortened obligations come due.
considered.reasoning: This replaces the static maturity-structure level with a credit-rationing event — the change in the long-term debt share — which is a different economic object: dlc/lt describes how a firm is financed, while a falling dltt/lt says lenders have just changed their willingness to fund it. It therefore reweights an entirely different set of firms than the three archived dlc/lt variants, including levered firms with stable short-term financing that the level conditioner always flags.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Corrected Funding Gap With Cash Earnings
considered.expression: WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(ADD(dlc, DELTA(SUB(act, che), 1)), ADD(che, ADD(pi, dp))), sale), 1)
considered.hypothesis: The near-term cash requirement is maturing debt plus the working capital the firm must fund, and the resources against it are cash on hand plus pretax income added back for depreciation — the standard non-cash charge — so a firm whose soft-asset absorption and debt maturities exceed its cash earnings must go outside for money.
considered.reasoning: This fixes a genuine accounting defect in the archive's best signal, where depreciation was netted against a change in *current* assets, an operation with no economic meaning; moving dp to the sources side as a non-cash add-back makes the construct an internally consistent cash-requirement identity. Using pretax income plus depreciation rather than oancf keeps coverage at balance-sheet/income-statement levels (the oancf version cost a third of the sample, dropping coverage to 0.071) and avoids the partial cancellation the critic noted, since oancf already embeds the working-capital change in the numerator.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Chronic Funding Gap
considered.expression: RANK(MA(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(ADD(dlc, SUB(DELTA(SUB(act, che), 1), dp)), che), sale), 1), 3))
considered.hypothesis: A one-year funding gap can reflect a lumpy investment or a single maturity; a gap sustained for three consecutive years identifies a business model that chronically consumes more cash than it generates and is therefore permanently dependent on refinancing at the market's discretion.
considered.reasoning: Averaging suppresses the year-specific measurement noise that likely flattens the gap's cross-sectional slope while retaining the persistent component that should drive a genuine distress premium, so it targets the fmb-versus-alpha disagreement with an economic rather than a cosmetic fix. It contrasts directly with the archived one-year level and one-year change, completing the level/change/persistence triple on the family's most successful construct.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Cash Needed While Lenders Shorten Maturity
considered.expression: MIN(ZSCORE(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(ADD(dlc, SUB(DELTA(SUB(act, che), 1), dp)), che), sale), 1)), ZSCORE(WINSOR(NEG(DELTA(RATIO(dltt, lt), 1)), 1)))
considered.hypothesis: A funding gap is only fatal if the credit market will not refinance it, so the firms to avoid are those that simultaneously need outside cash and are watching their lenders shift them out of long-dated into short-dated debt — demand for financing meeting a contraction in its supply.
considered.reasoning: The two legs come from independent data channels — a cash-requirement computation versus the maturity composition lenders impose — so unlike the archived MIN with ib−oancf there is no shared working-capital component to make attribution ambiguous. The credit-supply leg already produced a strong standalone slope (fmb = −2.84) while the gap produced the strongest alpha, and the conjunction demands both, which is exactly the state the economic story describes.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Liquidity Coverage After Accrual Absorption
considered.expression: WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(ADD(che, ADD(pi, dp)), DELTA(SUB(act, che), 1)), lct), 1)
considered.hypothesis: Express the accruals-distress state as a coverage ratio rather than a shortfall: cash on hand plus cash earnings, net of the cash swallowed by growth in soft working capital, measured against the obligations actually coming due; firms whose remaining coverage is high can absorb accrual reversals, and firms whose coverage is thin cannot.
considered.reasoning: This is a different functional form and a different sign convention from every archived signal — a bounded coverage multiple deflated by the claim base (lct is strictly positive and economically the right scale) rather than a shortfall deflated by a size proxy, which changes the cross-sectional shape that has been suppressing Fama-MacBeth slopes in the gap family. The accrual term enters as a drain on the numerator rather than as an additive requirement, so the construct rewards firms whose earnings arrive in cash and penalizes those whose earnings are absorbed by receivables and inventory.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Soft Assets Growing As Equity Erodes
considered.expression: MUL(ZSCORE(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(DELTA(SUB(act, che), 1), dp), at), 1)), RANK(NEG(GROWTH(ceq, 1))))
considered.hypothesis: A firm that is expanding receivables and inventory while its book equity is shrinking is consuming its loss-absorbing capital at the same time as it is increasing the pool of assets exposed to write-down, which is the classic pre-impairment configuration and the state in which auditors and lenders force recognition.
considered.reasoning: Equity erosion is a distress dimension the archive has never tested — every conditioner so far has been debt-side (leverage level, leverage change, maturity structure, credit supply) whereas this is the capital-account side, and shrinking ceq captures losses, buybacks-under-stress and write-offs that no liability ratio reveals. Because the conditioner is a growth rate of equity rather than a debt ratio, it reweights a different set of firms, including unlevered firms whose fragility is entirely earnings-driven.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Properly Netted Working Capital Accrual Under Liquidity Pressure
considered.expression: MUL(ZSCORE(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(DELTA(SUB(act, che), 1), DELTA(SUB(SUB(lct, dlc), txp), 1)), at), 1)), RANK(SUMRANK(RATIO(dlc, lt), NEG(RATIO(che, lct)))))
considered.hypothesis: The accrual that must be financed is the growth in non-cash current assets net of the growth in genuine operating liabilities — supplier and accrued-expense credit, excluding both debt and taxes payable — and it is this net financing requirement, not a depreciation-contaminated proxy, that becomes dangerous when short-dated debt and a thin cash buffer force asset conversion.
considered.reasoning: Every product-family signal in the archive nets fixed-asset depreciation against a current-asset change, an operation the critic correctly called economically meaningless, and separately the archive showed that dropping the liability side entirely destroyed the alpha; this specification keeps both sides of working capital and removes dp, so it identifies whether the family's power came from the correct accrual concept or from the mis-netting. Excluding taxes payable from the operating-liability side is deliberate, since tax deferrals reflect profitability and statutory timing rather than trade credit and were shown in generation 3 to carry the opposite sign.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Debt Shortfall Meeting Working Capital Absorption
considered.expression: MIN(ZSCORE(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(dlc, ADD(pi, dp)), sale), 1)), ZSCORE(WINSOR(RATIO(DELTA(SUB(act, che), 1), sale), 1)))
considered.hypothesis: The additive gap treats a dollar of maturing debt and a dollar of working-capital absorption as interchangeable, but the distress story says they must coincide: a firm whose cash earnings already fall short of its maturing debt and which is simultaneously pouring cash into receivables and inventory has no way to close the shortfall internally.
considered.reasoning: This decomposes the archive's best construct into its two economic pillars and requires both rather than summing them, which is a genuinely different functional form that will flag a different, smaller and more extreme set of firms than the additive gap. It also cleanly separates the two themes across legs — distress in the first, accruals in the second — so a strong result is unambiguously an interaction rather than a re-weighted single-theme effect.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Cash Requirement Without Retained Earnings Fallback
considered.expression: MUL(ZSCORE(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(ADD(dlc, DELTA(SUB(act, che), 1)), ADD(che, ADD(pi, dp))), sale), 1)), RANK(NEG(RATIO(re, at))))
considered.hypothesis: A cash shortfall is survivable for a firm with a deep stock of accumulated profits and lethal for one financed entirely by external capital, because the latter must return to markets on the market's terms; accumulated retained earnings are the fallback that determines whether a funding gap becomes a distress event.
considered.reasoning: Every conditioner tested on the accrual leg has been a flow or maturity variable, and retained earnings — the cumulative internal-capital stock — has never been paired with the funding-gap construct even though it is the classic Altman fragility term. Centering the gap leg keeps the retained-earnings rank as a pure slope modulator, so this asks whether the gap's −5.5% alpha is concentrated in firms with no earned-capital cushion.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Ranked Conjunction Of Cash Need And Credit Withdrawal
considered.expression: MIN(RANK(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(ADD(dlc, SUB(DELTA(SUB(act, che), 1), dp)), che), sale), 1)), RANK(NEG(DELTA(RATIO(dltt, lt), 1))))
considered.hypothesis: Financing demand meeting a contraction in financing supply is the sharpest distress state available in accounting data: the firm needs outside cash and its lenders are simultaneously refusing to term out its obligations.
considered.reasoning: The z-score version of this conjunction produced a significant alpha (−2.3%, t = −2.27) but a wrong-signed Fama-MacBeth slope (+1.01), which is the diagnostic signature of MIN being applied to two legs with very different scales and tail shapes so that one leg dominates the minimum almost everywhere. Taking the minimum of two uniform ranks makes the conjunction scale-free and genuinely symmetric, which should repair the cross-sectional slope while preserving the economically distinct credit-supply channel.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Full Near Term Claim Stack Versus Cash Earnings
considered.expression: WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(ADD(lct, DELTA(SUB(act, che), 1)), ADD(che, ADD(pi, dp))), sale), 1)
considered.hypothesis: Trade payables and accrued expenses are claims that come due within the year exactly like maturing debt, so the economically complete near-term claim stack is total current liabilities rather than short-term debt alone, and a firm whose cash earnings and cash balance cannot cover the whole stack plus its working-capital growth is the one that must refinance or liquidate.
considered.reasoning: The archive has only ever used dlc as the near-term claim, yet generation 3 showed that operating-liability growth carries the *opposite* sign to debt growth, so widening the claim base is a genuine and non-obvious test of whether all near-term claims are equivalent or whether financial claims are uniquely dangerous. If the broader stack performs worse, that pins the mechanism specifically on debt-market refinancing risk rather than on generic liquidity, which sharpens the interpretation of the whole family.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Fragility Score With Accrual Absorption Component
considered.expression: SUMRANK(RATIO(SUB(DELTA(SUB(act, che), 1), DELTA(SUB(SUB(lct, dlc), txp), 1)), at), SUMRANK(RATIO(dlc, lt), NEG(RATIO(re, at))))
considered.hypothesis: Distress scoring in the Altman-Ohlson tradition uses leverage and earned capital but ignores earnings quality entirely; a firm whose net working-capital absorption is high, whose debt is short-dated, and which has no accumulated retained earnings is fragile in three complementary ways, and accrual quality belongs inside the score as a component rather than as an external conditioner.
considered.reasoning: This is built from three raw accounting channels rather than from any archived expression, so it is not a rank-ensemble of previously evaluated signals, and its economic claim — that accrual absorption is a distress *ingredient*, not a distress-conditioned effect — is a structurally different proposition from everything in the archive. Ranking each channel before summing produces the bounded, well-behaved regressor the gap family has lacked, which targets the persistent Fama-MacBeth weakness while keeping three independent sources of return signal in the extreme deciles.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Accrual Discounted Current Ratio
considered.expression: WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(act, SUB(DELTA(SUB(act, che), 1), DELTA(SUB(SUB(lct, dlc), txp), 1))), lct), 1)
considered.hypothesis: The current ratio treats every dollar of current assets as equally good collateral, but the dollars added most recently through net working-capital build are the least proven — freshly extended receivables and unsold inventory recover least in a liquidation — so haircutting the newest accrual layer produces a distress ratio whose numerator reflects earnings quality.
considered.reasoning: Rather than demeaning an existing construct, this embeds the accrual measure *inside* a classic solvency ratio as a quality haircut, which is a functional form the archive has never tested and which cannot be decomposed into a distress term times an accrual term. It follows the strongest available evidence — the coverage ratio deflated by current liabilities delivered +5.5% alpha with t = +4.58 and a positive slope — while adding the accrual-quality adjustment that pure coverage lacks, and it uses only balance-sheet inputs so coverage stays near the archive maximum.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Cash Requirement As Credit Supply Contracts
considered.expression: MUL(ZSCORE(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(ADD(dlc, DELTA(SUB(act, che), 1)), ADD(che, ADD(pi, dp))), sale), 1)), RANK(NEG(DELTA(RATIO(dltt, lt), 1))))
considered.hypothesis: A funding gap is priced correctly when lenders remain willing to term out debt and is mispriced when they are withdrawing; a falling long-term share of liabilities reveals a supply-side judgment about the firm that the market has not yet impounded into equity prices.
considered.reasoning: Both conjunctive tests of this demand-meets-supply idea failed on the cross-section (fmb +1.01 and +0.71) because MIN lets one leg bind almost everywhere, yet the credit-supply leg has the strongest standalone slope of any conditioner in the archive (−2.84); the multiplicative slope-steepening form is the specification that has repeatedly delivered both metrics. This keeps a genuinely distinct economic channel alive — lender behavior rather than firm balance-sheet stocks — in the functional form the evidence says works.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Cash Requirement With Weak Debt Coverage
considered.expression: MUL(ZSCORE(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(ADD(dlc, DELTA(SUB(act, che), 1)), ADD(che, ADD(pi, dp))), sale), 1)), RANK(NEG(RATIO(ni, ADD(dlc, dltt)))))
considered.hypothesis: Credit markets do not judge fragility by asset-scaled leverage but by how many years of earnings it would take to retire the debt, so the state that turns an accrual-driven cash requirement into a distress event is a low earnings-to-total-debt multiple, which is exactly the covenant metric lenders actually write.
considered.reasoning: Every distress conditioner tested in this archive scales claims by assets, retained earnings or liability composition; none has used the earnings-coverage multiple that determines refinancing terms in practice, and firms with negative earnings automatically land at the fragile extreme with the correct ordering under NEG. Because the conditioner is denominated in debt rather than assets, it reweights asset-light firms with modest book leverage but no earnings — a group every asset-scaled ratio in the archive treats as safe.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Cash Requirement With Understated Depreciation
considered.expression: MUL(ZSCORE(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(ADD(dlc, DELTA(SUB(act, che), 1)), ADD(che, ADD(pi, dp))), sale), 1)), RANK(NEG(RATIO(dp, LAG(at, 1)))))
considered.hypothesis: A firm that must find cash and is simultaneously charging unusually little depreciation against its opening asset base is flattering the very cash-earnings figure that appears in its funding calculation, so its reported shortfall understates the true one and its assets carry unrecognized impairment.
considered.reasoning: Every conditioner in the archive is a balance-sheet or lender-behaviour state; this is the first that conditions on an *accounting choice*, asking whether the funding gap is most mispriced where the accounting inputs to it are themselves least conservative. It also rehabilitates the depreciation channel, which failed as a standalone leg (alpha −0.1%) but was never tested as a modifier of a construct that already works.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Quick Coverage After Net Accrual Absorption
considered.expression: WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(ADD(che, ADD(pi, dp)), SUB(DELTA(SUB(act, che), 1), DELTA(SUB(SUB(lct, dlc), txp), 1))), SUB(lt, dltt)), 1)
considered.hypothesis: The resources genuinely available to meet claims coming due are cash plus cash earnings minus the cash swallowed by net working-capital growth, and the claims are every liability that is not long-dated; a firm whose earnings arrive in cash covers this stack comfortably while one whose earnings are absorbed by receivables and inventory does not.
considered.reasoning: The critic correctly noted that including act in the numerator made the accrual haircut second-order; removing the current-asset stock entirely leaves a numerator in which the net accrual term is the same order of magnitude as cash earnings, so earnings quality genuinely drives the ratio. The archived coverage ratio built this way against current liabilities produced +5.5% alpha with t = +4.58, and this version adds the properly netted accrual (assets less operating liabilities, excluding taxes) and the complete non-long-term claim base.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Cash Requirement With Illiquid Asset Base
considered.expression: MUL(ZSCORE(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(ADD(dlc, DELTA(SUB(act, che), 1)), ADD(che, ADD(pi, dp))), sale), 1)), RANK(NEG(RATIO(act, at))))
considered.hypothesis: A firm facing a cash shortfall has one internal escape route — shrinking its own balance sheet — and that route is open only if its assets are current; a fixed-asset-heavy firm cannot liquidate its way out within the year and must go to lenders or shareholders on their terms.
considered.reasoning: Every conditioning variable tried so far sits on the right-hand side of the balance sheet — leverage, maturity, earned capital, lender behaviour — whereas this asks whether the asset side determines the severity of the same shortfall, which is a genuinely different economic question about self-help capacity. It is also close to orthogonal to the archive's conditioners, since capital-intensive firms are not systematically the ones with retained-earnings deficits or short-dated debt.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Cash Requirement Alongside Below The Line Charges
considered.expression: MUL(ZSCORE(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(ADD(dlc, DELTA(SUB(act, che), 1)), ADD(che, ADD(pi, dp))), sale), 1)), RANK(NEG(RATIO(SUB(ni, ib), at))))
considered.hypothesis: Discontinued operations, extraordinary items and other below-the-line charges are the accounting footprint of a restructuring already underway; a firm taking such charges while also running a cash shortfall is one where write-downs have begun but the working-capital overhang has not yet been cleared.
considered.reasoning: The difference between net income and income before extraordinary items is a distress marker that no signal in the archive has touched, and unlike chronic-loss indicators it is continuous and does not create a point mass, addressing the defect the critic identified in the previous version. It also captures a distinct timing state — the market may already know the firm is restructuring yet still misprice the unresolved accrual absorption sitting on its balance sheet.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Uniformized Coverage Without Earned Cushion
considered.expression: MUL(ZSCORE(RANK(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(ADD(che, ADD(pi, dp)), DELTA(SUB(act, che), 1)), lct), 1))), RANK(NEG(RATIO(re, at))))
considered.hypothesis: The mirror construct — cash and cash earnings surviving working-capital absorption, measured against obligations coming due — should reward firms whose earnings arrive in cash, and that reward should be largest for firms with no accumulated profits, because for them the coverage ratio is the only buffer that exists.
considered.reasoning: The unconditioned coverage ratio produced +5.5% alpha (t = +4.58) with a slope of only +1.77, exactly mirroring the gap family's imbalance, so applying the same two fixes — uniformization plus fragility conditioning — tests whether the diagnosis generalizes across a construct with a different deflator and the opposite sign. Confirming the mechanism on the mirror image is much stronger evidence than another variant on the same side of the ledger.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Cash Requirement Net Of Trade Credit
considered.expression: WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(ADD(dlc, SUB(DELTA(SUB(act, che), 1), DELTA(SUB(SUB(lct, dlc), txp), 1))), ADD(che, ADD(pi, dp))), sale), 1)
considered.hypothesis: Suppliers finance part of the working-capital build, so the cash a firm must actually raise is the growth in non-cash current assets *less* the growth in trade payables and accrued expenses; only the unfinanced residual represents a genuine external requirement.
considered.reasoning: Every version of this construct so far has counted the gross asset-side build as a cash need while the archive separately showed that operating-liability growth predicts *higher* returns, which is direct evidence that trade credit belongs on the sources side rather than being ignored. This is a change to what the signal measures rather than to how it is scaled or conditioned, and it should sharpen the identification of firms whose absorption is genuinely unfunded.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Abnormal Maturity Wall With Accrual Absorption
considered.expression: WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(ADD(SUB(dlc, MA(dlc, 3)), DELTA(SUB(act, che), 1)), ADD(che, ADD(pi, dp))), sale), 1)
considered.hypothesis: Firms with permanently high short-term debt run revolvers they roll as a matter of course, so the refinancing risk that matters is the *abnormal* portion of maturing debt relative to the firm's own recent norm, colliding with a working-capital drain and thin cash earnings.
considered.reasoning: Using the level of dlc treats a stable revolver borrower identically to a firm facing an unusual maturity wall, which plausibly dilutes the distress content of the requirement and contributes to the family's modest Sharpe ratios. Subtracting the firm's own three-year average of short-term debt keeps the accrual and cash-earnings terms as levels — they are genuinely current-period flows — while making only the debt term a deviation, which is the term whose level is a business-model constant.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Cash Requirement With Unpredictable Cash Earnings
considered.expression: MUL(ZSCORE(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(ADD(dlc, DELTA(SUB(act, che), 1)), ADD(che, ADD(pi, dp))), sale), 1)), RANK(VOL(RATIO(ADD(pi, dp), at), 5)))
considered.hypothesis: A cash shortfall is manageable when the resources that will close it are predictable and dangerous when they are not: firms whose cash earnings swing violently cannot plan around a maturity, cannot credibly commit to lenders, and are exactly the firms whose working-capital estimates are least reliable.
considered.reasoning: Every conditioner tested so far is a first-moment state — a leverage ratio, an earned-capital stock, a lender action, an asset mix — whereas this conditions on the second moment of the firm's cash-generating capacity, which is a distinct economic property that no balance-sheet ratio reveals and which is precisely what makes a funding requirement uninsurable. It also connects the two themes through uncertainty rather than through level fragility: volatile cash earnings imply volatile accruals, so the same conditioner rationalizes both the earnings-quality and the refinancing side of the story.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Absorption Rank Minus Cash Earnings Rank
considered.expression: SUB(RANK(WINSOR(RATIO(DELTA(SUB(act, che), 1), sale), 1)), RANK(WINSOR(RATIO(ADD(pi, dp), sale), 1)))
considered.hypothesis: The accruals-distress interaction can be expressed without any division as the distance between how aggressively a firm is absorbing cash into receivables and inventory and how strongly it is generating cash earnings; firms far up the absorption distribution and far down the cash-generation distribution are the fragile, low-quality-earnings cases.
considered.reasoning: This preserves the intensity idea the critic rejected while eliminating the denominator entirely, so there is no near-zero-scale artifact and no non-monotonicity — both legs are separately winsorized, sales-deflated and ranked before differencing. It is also a functional form the archive has never used: a signed rank spread, which is naturally bounded, symmetric and well behaved in a Fama-MacBeth regression, addressing the metric that has plateaued without relying on a monotone rescaling of an existing signal.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Cash Requirement At An Own History Liquidity Low
considered.expression: MUL(ZSCORE(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(ADD(dlc, DELTA(SUB(act, che), 1)), ADD(che, ADD(pi, dp))), sale), 1)), RANK(NEG(TS_RANK(RATIO(che, lct), 5))))
considered.hypothesis: Firms differ permanently in how much cash they hold, so the informative distress state is not the level of the cash buffer but whether the firm has drawn it down to the bottom of its own five-year range — a firm at its own liquidity low facing an accrual-driven cash requirement has already spent its reserves.
considered.reasoning: Every liquidity conditioner in the archive is cross-sectional (che/lct, dlc/lt), which confounds cash-rich business models with genuinely stressed firms; a within-firm position measure removes that permanent heterogeneity and isolates depletion, which is the economically active state. This is a different conditioning variable rather than a rescaling of an existing one, and because it is bounded in [0,1] by construction it cannot reintroduce the outlier problem that limits the family's cross-sectional slope.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Rank Space Funding Identity
considered.expression: SUMRANK(RATIO(DELTA(SUB(act, che), 1), sale), SUMRANK(RATIO(dlc, sale), NEG(RATIO(ADD(pi, dp), sale))))
considered.hypothesis: The cash-requirement identity — working-capital absorption plus maturing debt less cash earnings — is economically meaningful as an ordering of firms on each component, not as a dollar sum, so ranking the three terms separately before combining retains the full economics while removing the dominance of whichever term happens to be numerically largest.
considered.reasoning: The dollar-denominated identity yields alphas near −5.5% but slopes capped at −2.3, while the two-component rank spread yields a slope of −2.54 with no alpha, which localizes the problem precisely: rank space fixes the regression but the two-term spread discards the maturing-debt dimension that carries the portfolio payoff. This restores that third component in the same bounded space, which is the one specification the archive has never run and the only construction consistent with both diagnoses.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Cash Requirement While Revenue Contracts
considered.expression: MUL(ZSCORE(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(ADD(dlc, DELTA(SUB(act, che), 1)), ADD(che, ADD(pi, dp))), sale), 1)), RANK(NEG(GROWTH(sale, 1))))
considered.hypothesis: Working capital that expands while revenue shrinks cannot be justified by growth: the receivables were extended to buyers who are not returning and the inventory is not selling, so a cash requirement arising in a contracting business is the configuration in which the accrual will be written down rather than collected.
considered.reasoning: Every conditioner tested is a balance-sheet, lender, accounting-policy or cash-flow-moment variable; the demand environment in which the absorption occurred has never been used, even though it is the variable that determines whether soft assets convert to cash or to write-offs. Because the gap leg is demeaned and the conditioner bounded, this reweights growth-consistent absorption toward zero and concentrates the signal on firms whose accruals have no revenue justification.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Accelerating Working Capital Intensity Under Refinancing Pressure
considered.expression: MUL(ZSCORE(WINSOR(ACCEL(RATIO(SUB(SUB(act, che), SUB(SUB(lct, dlc), txp)), sale)), 1)), RANK(SUMRANK(RATIO(dlc, lt), NEG(RATIO(che, lct)))))
considered.hypothesis: A firm whose net working capital per dollar of revenue is not merely rising but rising at an increasing rate has lost control of its collection and inventory cycle, and that loss of control turns into a solvency problem when short-dated debt and a thin cash buffer force conversion on the firm's creditors' schedule rather than its own.
considered.reasoning: Every accrual leg in the archive is a level or a first difference; acceleration is a distinct economic state — deterioration that is itself worsening — and it identifies firms whose working-capital problem is compounding rather than one-off, which no level or change specification separates. Expressing it as intensity per unit of revenue and netting trade credit means the leg measures operating discipline rather than scale, and the liquidity conditioner supplies the distress channel that determines whether the compounding is survivable.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Deterioration From Own Best Cash Position
considered.expression: WINSOR(SUB(RATIO(SUB(ADD(dlc, DELTA(SUB(act, che), 1)), ADD(che, ADD(pi, dp))), sale), TS_MIN(RATIO(SUB(ADD(dlc, DELTA(SUB(act, che), 1)), ADD(che, ADD(pi, dp))), sale), 5)), 1)
considered.hypothesis: Each firm has demonstrated, at some point in the last five years, the tightest cash requirement its business model can achieve; the distance between today's requirement and that demonstrated best is a measure of how far the firm has drifted from its own attainable discipline, and drift of that kind is neither a business-model constant nor priced.
considered.reasoning: This uses a distance-from-extreme construction that the archive has never tested — the smoothing, first-difference and time-series-rank variants all measure something else, and unlike an ordinal position it retains cardinal information about how large the deterioration is. Because the benchmark is the firm's own historical minimum, capital intensity, margin and sector turnover are differenced out without any industry adjustment, which addresses the standing concern that the sales-deflated requirement embeds a business-model tilt.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Near Term Claim Intensity Including Committed Working Capital
considered.expression: WINSOR(RATIO(ADD(dlc, SUB(DELTA(SUB(act, che), 1), DELTA(SUB(SUB(lct, dlc), txp), 1))), lt), 1)
considered.hypothesis: What matters for refinancing is what fraction of a firm's whole obligation stack must be funded within the year, and that fraction includes not only debt maturing but the cash the firm has already committed to unfunded receivables and inventory; a firm with a long-dated liability structure can carry accruals that would sink a firm whose claims are front-loaded.
considered.reasoning: This is a maturity-structure measure rather than a shortfall measure — the two themes are combined inside a single fraction whose numerator is near-term cash claims from both accrual commitments and debt, and whose denominator is the entire liability stack — so it is neither a funding gap nor a coverage ratio and carries no cash-earnings or margin term at all. That absence is the point: it is the one construct in the family that cannot be confounded with the profitability anomaly, which has been an open objection to every sales-deflated version.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Free Cash Flow Coverage Of Interest Bearing Debt
considered.expression: WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(ADD(pi, dp), SUB(DELTA(SUB(act, che), 1), DELTA(SUB(SUB(lct, dlc), txp), 1))), ADD(dlc, dltt)), 1)
considered.hypothesis: The single number a credit analyst computes is free cash flow to total debt — cash earnings less the working capital they were consumed by, against the borrowings that must eventually be repaid — and equity prices should reward this quantity most where accruals have quietly eroded it.
considered.reasoning: The archive's coverage constructs all deflate by current or non-long-term liabilities and include the cash stock in the numerator, making them liquidity ratios; this is a pure flow-to-total-debt solvency multiple, a different economic quantity that ranks a cash-poor but strongly converting firm above a cash-rich but absorbing one. It keeps the accrual measure first-order in the numerator — net working-capital absorption is directly subtracted from cash earnings — so earnings quality drives the ratio rather than sitting as a second-order adjustment.
considered.author: proposer

critic_notes.target_name: Leveraged Total Accruals
critic_notes.rationale: Because the rank product is monotone in both legs it behaves close to an additive blend of two already-documented standalone predictors (Sloan accruals and leverage/distress) rather than isolating a genuine interaction, so any result will be hard to attribute to the conditioning story and it is the most obvious combination in this family.

critic_notes.target_name: Accruals Under Liquidity Squeeze
critic_notes.rationale: The inverted current ratio is a defensible short-horizon conditioning variable that is not itself a strong standalone return anomaly, though the rank-product form still leaves the accrual and liquidity main effects entangled and the design is structurally near-identical to the leverage version.

critic_notes.target_name: Accruals When Retained Earnings Are Negative
critic_notes.rationale: The indicator switch cleanly zeroes out the non-deficit subsample so any slope is attributable to the interaction rather than the baseline accrual effect, with the only real caveat being that the large mass of exact zeros sits mid-distribution and may distort decile portfolio composition.

critic_notes.target_name: Working Capital Accruals For Fragile Balance Sheets
critic_notes.rationale: Using the explicit non-cash working-capital accrual is a legitimate sharpening of the manipulation channel, but leverage and negative retained earnings are strongly collinear so the two-variable SUMRANK leg adds little beyond a single leverage cut, making this largely a refinement of the first two proposals.

critic_notes.target_name: Unstable Accruals In Weak Firms
critic_notes.rationale: Accrual volatility is a genuinely different construct from the accrual level and the distress interaction is economically motivated, though it flirts with the published accrual-quality/information-risk literature (whose return premium is contested and could plausibly carry the opposite sign) and the five-period VOL will cost coverage.

critic_notes.target_name: Accrual Gap Per Unit Of Debt Burden
critic_notes.rationale: Internally contradictory — dividing by total liabilities mechanically inflates the measure for LOW-liability (least distressed) firms, which the hypothesis itself concedes and then immediately claims the opposite, and stripped of that story it is just Sloan's accrual measure with an unstable deflator.

critic_notes.target_name: Receivable Inventory Build Under Leverage
critic_notes.rationale: The sign conventions on recch/invch are handled correctly and the ZSCORE-centering does isolate a slope-steepening interaction rather than a leverage tilt, but the construct is still fundamentally the Sloan accrual anomaly re-weighted by a distress proxy — a well-trodden conditioning that will need a large incremental t-stat over plain accruals to justify itself.

critic_notes.target_name: Supplier Credit Stretching In Deficit Firms
critic_notes.rationale: The sign-reversal hypothesis for payables in deficit firms is genuinely interesting, but the stated claim that "a negative slope can only come from the interaction" is false — the product of two uncentered [0,1] ranks loads heavily on both main effects, so the signal will largely reproduce the known low-retained-earnings/distress return effect unless at least one leg is demeaned.

critic_notes.target_name: Working Capital Accruals Only In Loss Firms
critic_notes.rationale: Masking the accrual measure to zero for the profitable majority creates a point mass covering most of the cross-section, which will make quantile sorts degenerate and the FF5 spread a thin loss-firm-only bet, and the underlying claim (accrual mispricing concentrated in loss/distressed firms) is already documented rather than novel.

critic_notes.target_name: Depreciation Shading By Levered Firms
critic_notes.rationale: A non-current-accrual manipulation channel is a legitimately different test from the working-capital variants and the centering is done properly, but DELTA(dp/sale) is dominated by movements in the sales denominator, so the signal risks being a repackaged sales-growth/asset-growth effect that happens to point the same direction — a fact the proposal never acknowledges.

critic_notes.target_name: Unpaid Taxes As Stealth Financing
critic_notes.rationale: The economic reading is ambiguous — a rising taxes-payable balance most commonly reflects higher current profitability, not involuntary deferral — and the construct compounds this with sparse/lumpy txp coverage and an uncentered rank product that again loads on the standalone distress main effect the authors claim to have neutralized.

critic_notes.target_name: Accrual Build Against Shrinking Sales
critic_notes.rationale: Receivable and inventory growth measured against contracting sales is essentially the Abarbanell-Bushee fundamental signals (inventory and receivables growth relative to sales growth) and the Thomas-Zhang inventory-change anomaly, so this is a direct rediscovery, further weakened by an uncentered rank product that mixes in the standalone accrual and sales-growth effects.

critic_notes.target_name: Balance Sheet Accruals Steepened By Leverage
critic_notes.rationale: The accrual leg is a textbook-correct Sloan (1996) balance-sheet accrual and the non-negative leverage RANK acts as a monotone reweighting, so the sort will be dominated by the published accrual anomaly (and its known amplification in distressed/constrained firms) rather than by a new cross-theme effect — though the coverage repair over generation 1's cash-flow lines is a legitimate fix.

critic_notes.target_name: Accruals While Leverage Is Rising
critic_notes.rationale: The trajectory-versus-level conditioning is a defensible and distinguishable lesson, but the two legs share a mechanical component (Δdlc enters both the accrual numerator and Δlt/at), so a positive result may partly reflect a squared debt-issuance effect rather than an accrual-conditioning effect and should be diagnosed accordingly.

critic_notes.target_name: Depreciation Lagging Asset Growth Under Leverage
critic_notes.rationale: NEG(GROWTH(dp) − GROWTH(at)) loads positively on asset growth, so with a negative expected sign the signal is largely a rediscovery of the asset-growth/investment anomaly (much of which FF5's CMA will absorb), and dp-growth ratios are additionally unstable for small-depreciation firms.

critic_notes.target_name: Accruals Against Rollover Pressure
critic_notes.rationale: Debt-maturity structure (dlc/lt) is a genuinely distinct conditioning dimension from leverage level, the liquidity-pressure mechanism matches the expression, and holding the accrual leg fixed against signal 1 makes the comparison interpretable — main caveat is that dlc/lt is noisy for financials and firms with tiny total liabilities.

critic_notes.target_name: Accrual Instability Premium In Fragile Firms
critic_notes.rationale: The positive expected sign is reverse-engineered from a single generation-1 alpha whose Fama-MacBeth slope was insignificant (t = 0.41), and it contradicts well-documented evidence that high earnings/accrual volatility and high distress both predict *lower* average returns, so this reads as sign-fitting rather than an independent risk test.

critic_notes.target_name: Industry Neutral Accrual Distress Interaction
critic_notes.rationale: This is a cosmetic neutralization variant of proposal 1 with no new economic content — industry demeaning is a standard preprocessing choice that should be applied within the better-motivated signals rather than consuming a separate proposal slot.

critic_notes.target_name: Accruals Against Cash Adjusted Rollover Pressure
critic_notes.rationale: A defensible but incremental sharpening of the archive's best signal — holding the accrual leg fixed while adding a cash-coverage dimension to the conditioner is a clean attribution test, though the added SUMRANK dimension may simply dilute the already-strong dlc/lt ranking rather than isolate a distinct economic state.

critic_notes.target_name: Soft Asset Build Under Rollover Pressure
critic_notes.rationale: This is the right test to run — stripping Δdlc from the accrual numerator directly addresses the mechanical double-counting concern while holding the conditioner fixed — though subtracting dp from a change in non-cash *current* assets is economically unmotivated (depreciation pertains to fixed assets) and should be dropped or justified.

critic_notes.target_name: Stabilized Accrual Burden On Equity Cushion
critic_notes.rationale: This is a transformation-only rerun of the archive's existing equity-cushion ratio signal (5% winsor plus industry demeaning), i.e. exactly the cosmetic variant the objective warns against, and the negligible FF5 alpha alongside a strong FMB slope more likely reflects a small-cap/microcap scaling artifact in the MAX(ceq,che) denominator than a fixable tail-instability problem.

critic_notes.target_name: Soft Assets Funded By Maturing Debt
critic_notes.rationale: A genuinely non-monotone conjunction with no shared mechanical terms between legs, and narrowing the funding leg from total debt issuance to short-maturity issuance is a substantive test of whether maturity mismatch (rather than external funding per se) is the active ingredient.

critic_notes.target_name: Operating Liability Stretch Under Rollover Pressure
critic_notes.rationale: Rebuilding the payables sign-flip from balance-sheet data to escape the 6% cash-flow-statement coverage is a legitimate fix, but because the conditioner is a non-negative rank the unconditional accrual main effect (which points the opposite way under standard Sloan logic) is not neutralized, so a null or wrong-signed result will be uninterpretable.

critic_notes.target_name: Pure Accrual Rollover Interaction
critic_notes.rationale: Swapping RANK for ZSCORE on the conditioning leg of the archive's best signal is a one-operator variant, and while the stated goal of isolating the cross-partial is analytically sensible, a product of two demeaned legs still does not identify an interaction without the main effects in the regression, so this is a diagnostic rather than a new mechanism.

critic_notes.target_name: Ranked Near Term Funding Gap
critic_notes.rationale: RANK is a monotone transform of the already-archived "Near Term Funding Gap," so the decile sort and every portfolio statistic are mechanically unchanged and only the Fama-MacBeth number moves — this is a cosmetic re-specification of an evaluated signal rather than a new construct, and the winsorized ratio's tail contamination could equally be diagnosed without consuming a proposal slot.

critic_notes.target_name: Funding Gap Net Of Internal Cash Generation
critic_notes.rationale: Adding operating cash flow to the sources term is a genuine economic change that converts a balance-sheet snapshot into an external-financing need, but the proposal understates that oancf already embeds the working-capital change appearing in the numerator's accrual term, so part of the "improvement" is a partial cancellation of the soft-asset leg rather than a clean addition.

critic_notes.target_name: Widening Funding Gap
critic_notes.rationale: The level-versus-change question is well motivated by the archive's rising-leverage result and does purge persistent capital-intensity effects, but because the level already contains DELTA(act−che), this is effectively a second difference of working capital deflated by a moving sales base, which is likely to be dominated by measurement noise.

critic_notes.target_name: Unbacked Earnings Meeting A Funding Gap
critic_notes.rationale: The MIN conjunction is correctly signed (high only when both legs are high) and the interaction with a funding-gap state is not a plain accruals rediscovery, but the claim of "no mechanical overlap" is simply wrong — ib−oancf is the standard cash-flow accrual measure and shares its working-capital component with the gap leg — so any incremental power over the gap alone will be hard to attribute.

critic_notes.target_name: Accruals Against Maturity And Coverage Pressure
critic_notes.rationale: This is the third variant of the same accrual-leg-times-dlc/lt conditioner, differing from the archived "Accruals Against Cash Adjusted Rollover Pressure" only by swapping the cash-stock buffer (che/lct) for a flow coverage term (oancf/lt) inside the same SUMRANK, which is the kind of one-input cosmetic tweak the objective explicitly discourages.

critic_notes.target_name: Accrual Turbulence Under Rollover Pressure
critic_notes.rationale: The U-shape hypothesis is a genuinely different structural claim and worth one clean test against the archive's best conditioner, but the prior is unfavorable — the archived ABS-based opacity signal under fragility produced a significantly *wrong*-signed alpha (+3.5%, t=2.64), and discarding sign throws away the information driving the −3.7 t-stat on the signed version.

critic_notes.target_name: Funding Gap Plus Conditioned Accrual Composite
critic_notes.rationale: This is a mechanical rank-ensemble of two already-archived signals whose legs share dlc, the soft-asset change and dp, so it adds no new economic mechanism and its attribution will be ambiguous — the archive already contains a SUMRANK blend of the same family.

critic_notes.target_name: Corrected Funding Gap With Cash Earnings
critic_notes.rationale: The accounting fix (moving dp from a nonsensical netting against ΔCurrent Assets to the sources side) is legitimate and internally consistent, but subtracting pi/sale embeds a pretax-margin term that risks the signal degenerating into the well-known profitability anomaly, so any improvement must be shown to survive a margin control.

critic_notes.target_name: Corrected Funding Gap Per Dollar Of Assets
critic_notes.rationale: A pure deflator swap on the immediately preceding proposal is the definition of a cosmetic variant; it is defensible as a diagnostic but is not a substantively different construct and should be run as a robustness check on signal 2 rather than proposed as a separate signal.

critic_notes.target_name: Chronic Funding Gap
critic_notes.rationale: Three-year smoothing of the archive's strongest construct is a standard but economically motivated persistence transform that directly targets the fmb-versus-alpha disagreement, though it is incremental and inherits the uncorrected dp-netting defect flagged in proposal 2.

critic_notes.target_name: Cash Needed While Lenders Shorten Maturity
critic_notes.rationale: The conjunction of financing demand (gap) with a credit-supply contraction (falling long-term liability share) draws on genuinely distinct data channels and neither leg has been tested against the other, making this the most economically substantive proposal in the batch — though MIN of z-scores is scale-sensitive and both archived MIN constructs delivered weak Fama-MacBeth slopes.

critic_notes.target_name: Funding Gap At Its Own Five Year Extreme
critic_notes.rationale: This is one of the two legs of the already-evaluated peers-plus-history composite rather than a new signal; the decomposition is informative but with annual data a five-period TS_RANK is very coarse, so it belongs as an attribution check on the archived result, not a fresh proposal.

critic_notes.target_name: Two Pillar Cash Requirement And Accrual Slope Score
critic_notes.rationale: This is a mechanical rank-ensemble of two verbatim archived expressions ("Corrected Funding Gap With Cash Earnings" and "Accruals Against Cash Adjusted Rollover Pressure") whose heavily overlapping inputs guarantee a blended, largely predictable result rather than a new mechanism or a diagnosis of why the two disagree.

critic_notes.target_name: Industry Relative Cash Requirement
critic_notes.rationale: Industry demeaning of an already-tested construct is a standard neutralization rather than a substantively different signal, and while the margin/turnover confound it targets is real, the proposal is single-theme (no accrual–distress interaction remains) and sits close to the "cosmetic variant" line the objective warns against.

critic_notes.target_name: Debt Shortfall Meeting Working Capital Absorption
critic_notes.rationale: The conjunctive MIN form is a genuinely different functional specification from the additive gap, the sign logic is internally consistent (both legs high ⇒ high MIN ⇒ predicted underperformance), and it cleanly isolates distress in one leg and accrual absorption in the other; the main caveat is that the −(pi+dp)/sale term still imports a profitability tilt.

critic_notes.target_name: Cash Requirement Without Retained Earnings Fallback
critic_notes.rationale: The expression matches the hypothesis (a positive rank multiplier steepens the gap slope for low earned-capital firms) and retained earnings has not previously been paired with the funding-gap leg, but the MUL(z, RANK(conditioner)) template is heavily reused in this archive and re/at is itself a well-known distress/profitability predictor, so incremental content is modest.

critic_notes.target_name: Ranked Conjunction Of Cash Need And Credit Withdrawal
critic_notes.rationale: Because MIN is not invariant to monotone rescaling, replacing z-scores with ranks genuinely changes which leg binds and is a defensible repair of the archived version's wrong-signed slope, but the economic content is unchanged from "Cash Needed While Lenders Shorten Maturity" so this is a methodological retry rather than a new idea and should be judged strictly against that weak baseline.

critic_notes.target_name: Full Near Term Claim Stack Versus Cash Earnings
critic_notes.rationale: Swapping dlc for lct is a one-input variant, but it is a discriminating test with informative value in either direction given the archive's evidence that operating-liability growth carries the opposite sign; the risk is that lct embeds the payables/accruals component with a sign opposite to the intended distress reading, muddying interpretation of an inconclusive result.

critic_notes.target_name: Cash Requirement Without Capital Or Earned Cushion
critic_notes.rationale: This is a cosmetic conditioner swap on the archived "Cash Requirement Without Retained Earnings Fallback," replacing RANK(NEG(re/at)) with the RANK(SUMRANK(lt/at, NEG(re/at))) composite that has already been used as a conditioner earlier in the archive, and since lt/at and −re/at are strongly correlated the reweighting is unlikely to be economically informative about which channel drives the amplification.

critic_notes.target_name: Cash Requirement As Credit Supply Contracts
critic_notes.rationale: The credit-supply conditioner (falling long-term liability share) is a genuinely distinct, lender-side channel that has only ever been combined with the funding gap via MIN — a form the archive shows fails on the cross-section — so testing the multiplicative slope-steepening version with the corrected cash-earnings gap is a substantive, well-diagnosed next step rather than a relabeling.

critic_notes.target_name: Chronic Cash Requirement Without Earned Cushion
critic_notes.rationale: Mechanically stacking two already-tested modifications (MA(3) smoothing of the gap, which collapsed the slope, and the re/at conditioner, which preserved it) is a variant-combination rather than a new mechanism, and the most likely outcome is an interpolation between two known results with no new economic content.

critic_notes.target_name: Accrual Discounted Claim Coverage
critic_notes.rationale: The numerator is dominated by act, so the signal is essentially a current/short-term-claim coverage ratio — a long-known liquidity/distress measure — with a second-order accrual haircut that is far too small relative to total current assets to carry the earnings-quality mechanism the hypothesis claims.

critic_notes.target_name: Additive Rank Score Of Cash Need And Deficit
critic_notes.rationale: The hypothesis is about functional form rather than economics, and it is internally inconsistent — a rank sum removes the interaction entirely and therefore cannot "capture the same economics as multiplying the gap by the deficit rank" — while additive rank composites of these exact inputs are already represented in the archive's fragility-score family.

critic_notes.target_name: Cash Requirement In Chronically Lossmaking Firms
critic_notes.rationale: The reasoning is factually wrong about its own construction — multiplying by MA(INDICATOR(...),3) sets the signal to exactly zero for every firm with no loss years, creating precisely the large mid-distribution point mass it claims to avoid — and the chronic-weak-profitability conditioner it revives is already archived as a generation-1 failure.

critic_notes.target_name: Uniformized Cash Requirement Without Earned Cushion
critic_notes.rationale: This is the archive's "Cash Requirement Without Retained Earnings Fallback" with a rank transform inserted ahead of the z-score — a monotone rescaling of one leg, i.e. exactly the cosmetic variant the objective warns against, and the claim that outlier leverage points are what caps the FMB slope is asserted rather than diagnosed.

critic_notes.target_name: Uniformized Coverage Without Earned Cushion
critic_notes.rationale: Internally consistent (a centered coverage leg scaled by a positive fragility rank preserves the positive expected sign) and it fills the untested cell of the coverage×conditioner grid, but the novelty is limited to recombining two archive components plus the same rank rescaling, so it is a weak test of the stated "distributional" diagnosis.

critic_notes.target_name: Cash Requirement Net Of Trade Credit
critic_notes.rationale: This changes what is measured rather than how it is scaled — moving supplier and accrued-expense growth to the sources side of the funding identity — and the motivation is directly grounded in the archive's finding that operating-liability builds predicted higher returns, so the expression, hypothesis and expected sign all line up.

critic_notes.target_name: Abnormal Maturity Wall With Accrual Absorption
critic_notes.rationale: Replacing the short-term debt level with its deviation from the firm's own three-year norm is an economically defensible attempt to separate routine revolver rolling from a genuine maturity wall, though it discards the level of near-term debt burden (itself informative) and mixes a demeaned term with level terms in the same sum, so the sign is less clean than claimed.

critic_notes.target_name: Share Of Cash Earnings Consumed By Working Capital
critic_notes.rationale: This is close to a re-run of the already-tested "Accrual Build Per Dollar Of Equity Cushion" with the cushion swapped for cash earnings, and the stated safeguard is wrong — MAX(pi+dp, che) can still approach zero for cash-poor, marginally profitable firms and makes the signal a non-monotone, denominator-driven artifact rather than a clean accrual-intensity measure.

critic_notes.target_name: Uniformized Cash Requirement With Weak Debt Coverage
critic_notes.rationale: Direct rediscovery of the archive's "Cash Requirement With Weak Debt Coverage" with the same rank rescaling proposed in signal 1, making it doubly redundant and offering no new economic content.

critic_notes.target_name: Rank Space Funding Identity
critic_notes.rationale: The rank-space recasting of the three-component funding identity is a substantively different construction from the archived dollar gap and the two-term rank spread, and the directional logic is internally consistent, though the nested SUMRANK silently assigns half the weight to working-capital absorption and only a quarter each to maturing debt and cash earnings, which contradicts the stated "rank the three terms separately" motivation and should be flattened.

critic_notes.target_name: Cash Requirement With No Cushion And Volatile Earnings
critic_notes.rationale: This is a cosmetic recombination of two conditioners already separately tested on the identical base gap (re/at at −5.9%/−4.93 and cash-earnings volatility at −5.6%/−4.96), and since the unconditioned gap itself already delivers −5.5%/−5.07, the proposal has essentially no room to be informative about mechanism regardless of outcome.

critic_notes.target_name: Unfunded Cash Requirement Without Earned Cushion
critic_notes.rationale: Crossing the archive's trade-credit-netted numerator (−5.2%, t −4.59) with the archive's re/at conditioner (−5.9%, t −4.93) is a mechanical two-piece consolidation whose expected result is indistinguishable from either parent and from the unconditioned gap, so it tests no new economic proposition.

critic_notes.target_name: Netted Quick Coverage Without Earned Cushion
critic_notes.rationale: This is effectively a rediscovery of two archived signals at once — "Quick Coverage After Net Accrual Absorption" (t +4.62) and "Uniformized Coverage Without Earned Cushion" (t +4.48) — and the proposal's own reasoning concedes it is a robustness re-run rather than a new hypothesis.

critic_notes.target_name: Cash Requirement While Revenue Contracts
critic_notes.rationale: The demand-side conditioner is genuinely absent from the archive and supplies the missing economic determinant of whether soft assets convert to cash or write-offs, with a consistent sign; the main caveat is partial mechanical overlap, since falling sales inflates the sales-deflated gap directly and low sales growth is itself a known positive-return characteristic working against the expected sign.

critic_notes.target_name: Cash Requirement Plus Absorption Cash Earnings Spread
critic_notes.rationale: This is a rank-sum ensemble of two signals already in the archive, and the stated defense is factually wrong — the second leg is verbatim the archived "Absorption Rank Minus Cash Earnings Rank" — so the construction is exactly the kind of ensemble-of-tested-signals that cannot separate which representation the market misprices.
